intro: Low-rank compression keeps the matrix directions carrying the most energy. Reconstruct the approximation and measure the discarded energy separately.
task: Return a rank-limited matrix reconstruction and its squared Frobenius residual using the largest singular values.
requirements: matrix is a nonempty matrix. rank is an integer from zero through min(matrix.shape).
Return {"matrix": approximation, "squared_error": sum((matrix-approximation)**2)}. Rank zero returns a zero matrix.
When 0<rank<min(shape), reject a positive boundary singular value above 1e-12 if its gap to the retained value is at most 1e-10; otherwise the best approximation can be ambiguous.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Singular values rank the strength of matrix directions. Reconstruct only the leading terms of the expansion.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Report the residual energy after reconstruction; a tie at the cutoff makes a unique best reconstruction impossible.

explanation: The truncated singular-value expansion is a best rank-k approximation in squared Frobenius error. Its discarded squared singular values equal the residual energy.

Singular-vector signs cancel during reconstruction. A tie exactly at the truncation boundary is different: several reconstructed matrices can be equally good, so this contract rejects that ambiguous case.
